sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: the GitLab project https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr , the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/ and the r-universe page https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/robotstxtr . The GitHub copy (github.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr) is a read-only mirror, also HTTPS-only.
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README give a clear, succinct description of what robotstxtr does (engine-aware robots.txt policy evaluation using a bundled snapshot of Google's C++ matcher): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr#readme
interact_justification: The pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/ explains how to obtain the package (README installation section), links the bug tracker ("Report a bug"), the contributing guide (https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/CONTRIBUTING.html) and the code of conduct.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) opens by explaining how to report bugs and request features in the GitLab issue tracker and how to send changes: as merge requests on GitLab (the GitHub repository is a read-only mirror). It then states what a merge request needs: tests for new code, one NEWS.md bullet per user-facing change, and a passing verification command.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions: a clean lintr run against the goodpractice-aligned .lintr set, R CMD check --as-cran in the pre-push verify chain, and regenerated man/ and NAMESPACE committed with the change (checked by scripts/check-docs-drift.R): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: DESCRIPTION declares License: MIT + file LICENSE; LICENSE and the full text in LICENSE.md are at the repository top level (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/LICENSE.md), with the vendored Apache-2.0 matcher's terms in inst/NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
floss_license_justification: Released under the MIT license; the bundled Google matcher is Apache-2.0: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/LICENSE.md
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT and Apache-2.0 are OSI-approved open source licenses: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: The pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/ carries the README (installation and use), the introduction vignette (https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/articles/introduction.html) and the function reference; the engine-aware contract is documented in design/engine-contract-v1.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/design/engine-contract-v1.md
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented with roxygen2 man pages, published as the reference at https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/reference/ .
repo_public_justification: Public GitLab repository: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr . The GitHub repository is a read-only mirror.
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique version in DESCRIPTION and a matching tag (v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tags
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning; release tags at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tags
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git (v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tags
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab work items serve as the public issue tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items), linked as "Report a bug" on the pkgdown site https://bart-turczynski.gitlab.io/robotstxtr/ . DESCRIPTION names the same tracker as BugReports by its legacy /-/issues address, the form R's CRAN incoming check requires.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unacknowledged: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed on the public tracker to date (0 issues on 2026-10-03), so none is unanswered: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy, https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md , which CONTRIBUTING.md points to: reports go to the maintainer by email, with a confidential GitLab issue as a documented alternative, never a public issue. It also states the supported versions, what to expect (acknowledgment within 7 days, coordinated disclosure) and the scope. SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml links it as the policy and names the same contact in machine-readable form.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md) documents two confidential channels: email to bartek@turczynski.pl, and a GitLab issue submitted with "This issue is confidential" ticked, visible only to the reporter, assignees and project members allowed to see confidential issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received through GitLab in the last 6 months (0 issues, confidential ones included, on 2026-10-03); SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 7 days: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools) and a C++17 compiler for the bundled matcher, wired by src/Makevars: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/src/Makevars
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling and a C++17 compiler; no external system libraries.
build_floss_tools_justification: R, GCC/Clang, and the entire build toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_justification: Automated test suite using testthat (edition 3), including the upstream matcher cases and the Bing and Yandex conformance corpora, with all network access mocked or served locally: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with testthat::test_local() or devtools::test(), and as part of R CMD check; the full pre-push chain is dev/verify.sh and the CI gates are Rscript dev/gates.R: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/dev/verify.sh
test_most_justification: covr measures coverage in the coverage CI job on every push to main and reports it through GitLab's coverage reporting; the main pipeline of 2026-09-30 measured 95.29% line coverage of the package's own code (the vendored upstream matchers are excluded by .covrignore and validated by their conformance corpora): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/jobs/16850798923
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the policy: new code needs tests (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). In practice behavioral commits ship with a test file named for the tracker issue they close (e.g. test-resolve-matcher-profile-nvuwpktu.R, test-nul-body-hcqrzikz.R): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality and fixes ship with tests; recent feat and fix commits on main each add or change tests/testthat files: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, the instructions for change proposals, states that new code needs tests and that a merge request must pass the verification command, which runs the test suite: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: lintr, R CMD check --as-cran and the C++ compiler warnings it reports surface in dev/verify.sh (the pre-push hook) and in the gates and check CI jobs on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: The verification chain and the check CI job fail on any R CMD check warning, and lint fails on any lint, so warnings are fixed before a push lands.
warnings_strict_justification: CI sets LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT=true so any lint fails, and the check job runs rcmdcheck with error_on = "warning"; dev/verify.sh applies the same rules before every push: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles: robots.txt bodies and URLs are untrusted input; fetches refuse non-http(s) schemes, private and special-purpose destinations (SSRF guard) and https-to-http downgrades, forward no credentials or cookies, and bound body size and time: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/R/fetch-policy.R
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common pitfalls for this package: C++ memory safety in the bundled matchers, NUL bytes and invalid encodings in bodies, SSRF through redirects and alternate IP spellings, and matcher parser differentials; each has dedicated tests (test-nul-body, test-ssrf, the upstream and corpus conformance suites).
crypto_published_justification: robotstxtr implements no cryptography; its only cryptographic protocol is TLS for https fetches, performed by libcurl through httr2. TLS is a published, publicly reviewed protocol.
crypto_call_justification: robotstxtr re-implements no cryptography: https is delegated to httr2, libcurl and its TLS backend.
crypto_floss_justification: The cryptography robotstxtr relies on (TLS through libcurl, e.g. with OpenSSL) is implementable with FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: robotstxtr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_working_justification: robotstxtr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_pfs_justification: robotstxtr implements no key agreement; TLS key exchange is negotiated by the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_password_storage_justification: robotstxtr stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: robotstxtr does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: robotstxtr selects no algorithms, ciphers or key lengths; TLS parameters are those of the user's libcurl and TLS backend.
crypto_used_network_justification: robots_fetch() fetches robots.txt from the origin of the URL the caller supplies, over http or https as given. It allows http-to-https upgrades and refuses https-to-http downgrades, but plain http origins are fetched over http.
crypto_tls12_justification: https fetches go through httr2 and libcurl with its TLS backend, which support TLS 1.2 and later; robotstxtr never sets or lowers the TLS version: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/R/fetch-policy.R
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: robotstxtr leaves libcurl's certificate and host-name verification at their defaults, which are on, and classifies a verification failure as a TLS error rather than retrying without it: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/R/fetch-policy.R
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: robotstxtr sends no Authorization, cookies or caller session state, and for https libcurl completes certificate verification in the TLS handshake before any HTTP header is sent: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/R/fetch-policy.R
delivery_mitm_justification: robotstxtr is installed from r-universe (https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/robotstxtr) or GitLab (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr), both over HTTPS only.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Installation fetches sources and binaries from r-universe or GitLab over HTTPS. The project publishes no separate hash or signature files, so no cryptographic hash is served over an unencrypted channel: https://bart-turczynski.r-universe.dev/robotstxtr
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items
static_analysis_justification: lintr (a full-package lint using the goodpractice-aligned set in .lintr) and R CMD check, including the compiler's warnings on the C++ sources, run in the pre-push chain and in the gates and check CI jobs on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: lintr and R CMD check find defects but are not vulnerability scanners, and no vulnerability-focused analyzer (such as a C/C++ SAST tool) runs over src/. The osv-audit and security-audit jobs check dependencies against OSV and OSS Index on a weekly schedule, but that is SCA, not static analysis of robotstxtr's code: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The verification chain fails on any lintr finding or R CMD check warning, so static-analysis findings are fixed before a push lands.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every push: dev/verify.sh, the pre-push hook, runs it, and the gates CI job runs it again on every push to main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Before a CRAN submission the package is checked, test suite included, on R-hub's platforms (release checklist step 6, whose robotstxtr deltas in CONTRIBUTING.md single out the sanitizers and valgrind for the compiled code). For 0.3.0, clang-asan (AddressSanitizer) and clang-ubsan (UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer) reported no findings, as recorded in cran-comments.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/cran-comments.md
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: robotstxtr ships C++ in src/ (the bundled Google, Bing and Yandex matchers and their bindings). AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer runs on R-hub cover it before each submission (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/cran-comments.md). They run per release, not on every push.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: robotstxtr's testthat expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime on every run of the verification chain and the check CI job: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/tree/main/tests/testthat
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The sanitizer runs for 0.3.0 reported no findings in robotstxtr's code; R-hub's valgrind job failed for a platform reason, with no frame in robotstxtr code, as recorded in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The GitLab CI pipeline (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/pipelines) runs the gates (lint, README and docs drift, vendored-matcher fidelity), the citation check, R CMD check --as-cran with the test suite, and coverage on every push to main (configuration: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml). Branch pushes and merge requests start no pipeline; the same verification chain runs as a pre-push hook on every branch.
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/work_items
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed. A gitleaks scan of the full git history (182 commits across all refs, 2026-10-03) reported one finding, a false positive: the string "assumed_rfc9309" in tests/testthat/test-cross-engine-separation-pdcrkcvq.R, matched by the generic-api-key rule: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr#readme
hardening_justification: robotstxtr applies no hardening of its own. Its C++ is compiled with the flags of the user's R installation (src/Makevars sets only the C++ standard, include paths and build definitions: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/blob/main/src/Makevars), so stack protection or _FORTIFY_SOURCE apply only where that R build turns them on.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab, r-universe) manage their own authentication; robotstxtr operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: release 0.3.0 tagged 2026-09-28 and frequent commits on main: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/robotstxtr/-/commits/main
